바울의 마지막 전도여행 코스: Route of Paul's Last Missionary Journey
1. 바울의 마지막 전도여행 코스\n 1) 로마감옥에서 풀려난 후 그레데:
1. Route of Paul's Last Missionary Journey
 1) After being released from the Roman prison he goes to Crete
 -**Rome (Emperor Nero died, so the apostle Paul was released). Released, found not guilty. And originally he wanted to go to Spain, right? But it doesn't look like he went to Spain. He came straight over, arrived in Crete, visited the church and left Titus behind (Titus 1:5, he left Titus there).  He leaves people like Apollos and Zenas the lawyer behind.
 2) He goes to Ephesus and leaves Timothy behind **Ephesus (1 Tim 1:3, he tells Timothy to stay in Ephesus).
 3) **Colossae (Phlm 1:22, prepare me a lodging).**Hierapolis, Laodicea (Col 4:13).
 - He would have gone through Laodicea to the Colossae area and visited Philemon's house. In the letter to Philemon he said he'd come and see whether Philemon had welcomed Onesimus well and forgiven him, so of course he would have gone.
 - Then he went to Hierapolis, and passed through Smyrna, Pergamum, Adramyttium and Assos, and arrived in Troas. It was getting a bit hot by then, so he took off his cloak and left it at the house of a deacon named Carpus. Because in 2 Tim chapter 4 he asks for the cloak he left at Carpus's house to be brought.
<딤후4:13> 네가 올 때에 내가 드로아 가보의 집에 둔 겉옷을 가지고:
<2 Tim 4:13> The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, when you come, bring with you, and the books, especially the parchments
  - So he crossed over to Samothrace, crossed over to Neapolis, and reached Philippi.
**Philippi (Phil 2:24 “But I trust in the Lord that I myself also will come shortly”) He would have looked into the problems of the Philippian church.. And while he was sorting out the church problems like that, he needed to go back to Ephesus and appoint elders and deacons, but he writes a letter to Timothy in Ephesus saying, ‘In case I'm late, you appoint them instead.’ That's 1 Timothy
 5) He crosses over to the region of Achaia and sends the letter to Titus
 - Then he went through Amphipolis and Apollonia, and when he got to around Thessalonica, there were problems there too.
 - Paul thought, this won't do, and sends a letter to Titus. Right after writing to Timothy he writes to Titus, and that is the book of Titus. It also deals with the issue of appointing elders.
 6) Gathers at Nicopolis, then after going to prison he writes 2 Timothy and is martyred
<딛3:12~14> 내가 아데마나 두기고를 네게 보내리니 그 때에 네가:
<Titus 3:12~14> When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there. Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey speedily, that nothing may be lacking for them. Let our people also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they may not be unfruitful
 - When he writes and sends the letter to Titus, he says: depending on how things go here I'll send Artemas or Tychicus, so when they arrive hurry over, and if people like Apollos or Zenas the lawyer don't have anything to do, send them ahead first. So they learn to get the meetings ready ahead of time. That's what he's writing about.
 - In Troas it was hot, but by the time he gets around here it's already winter, so he says he's decided to spend the winter in Nicopolis. It looks like he was probably planning a big gathering.
 - But there's no record that the gathering happened, and a little later we can see Paul is in prison in Rome. Something went wrong, who knows what, but anyway he's locked up in a Roman prison
이 때 감옥은 가택연금이 아니라 사형수 감옥인 마메틴 감옥이다. 돌로 쪼: The prison this time is not house arrest; it's the Mamertine prison, a prison for those sentenced to death. A prison cut out of stone. It's designed in a strange way, with just one small window, and when you look out of it, all you can see is the road to the execution ground. The letter he wrote at this time is 2 Timothy.
딤전, 딛, 딤후 - 목회자가 목회자에게 보냈다 해서 목회 서신으로 분류: 1 Tim, Titus, 2 Tim - because they were sent by a pastor to pastors, they're classified as the Pastoral Epistles. Overall they write about serving the church, appointing deacons and elders, and the work a pastor has to do.
